The Company targets commercial banking clients within its primary market area for loan originations and deposit growth, including businesses, professionals and wealth-building individuals.
The strategic plan is intended to enhance earnings, reduce interest rate risk and provide a broader range of financial services to clients and the local communities the Company serves.

Although the Company intends to prudently increase the percentage of its assets consisting of higher-yielding commercial real estate, real estate construction and commercial business loans, which offer higher risk-adjusted returns, shorter maturities and more sensitivity to interest rate fluctuations, the Company intends to manage credit exposure through the use of experienced bankers in these areas and a…

The Company’s ability to continue to attract and retain banking professionals with strong community relationships and significant knowledge of its markets will be a key to its success.

The Company adjusts its investments in liquid assets based upon management’s assessment of (i) expected loan demand, (ii) projected loan sales, (iii) expected deposit flows, (iv) yields available on interest-bearing deposits and (v) asset/liability management objectives.
The Company anticipates that it will have sufficient funds available to meet current loan commitments.

The Company evaluates capital expenditure projects based on a variety of factors, including expected strategic impacts (such as forecasted impact on revenue growth, productivity, expenses, service levels and client retention) and its expected return on investment.

Based on its current capital allocation objectives, during the remainder of fiscal 2027 the Company expects cash expenditures of approximately $1.7 million for capital investment in premises and equipment.

Management currently expects to continue the Company’s current practice of paying quarterly cash dividends on its common stock subject to the Board of Directors’ discretion to modify or terminate this practice at any time and for any reason without prior notice.

Future impairment charges could occur if adverse events or changes in circumstances arise, including, but not limited to: (i) a sustained decline in the Company’s stock price or that of peer institutions, (ii) revenue declines beyond current forecasts, or (iii) significant adverse changes in the operating environment for the financial industry.

The absence of a provision in the current periods reflected the continued adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, as determined through management’s evaluation of economic forecast assumptions and other qualitative and quantitative factors.
The ACL remained relatively stable year over year, reflecting the continued strength of the loan portfolio and management's assessment of expected credit losses.
Management continues to closely monitor the identified credit relationships and does not currently anticipate losses beyond those already reflected in the ACL.

State and local taxes increased by $113,000 and $231,000 for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, primarily due to higher business and occupation taxes resulting from changes in state tax requirements and increased sales tax activity related to projects supporting the Company's strategic initiatives.
